title: session-mosaic-length-concurrency-grid-draft
content:
Sessionized Cost-Latency Mosaic: conversational prompt-length x concurrency grid — draft explainer

Purpose
- Quick explainer and human-readable collateral for the internal perf playbook: show how per-session prompt length and live concurrency interact to produce non-linear latency and cost regimes. Target audience: SREs, platform eng, product Optimize, and solutions engineering.

Short summary findings (top-level)
- Small prompts (<=32 tokens) are latency-dominated at low concurrency; batching yields poor marginal savings until concurrency >= 8.
- Mid-length prompts (128–512 tokens) show the largest delta: latency improves with batching, and amortized cost per output token drops 20–45% in the 4–16 concurrency window.
- Long prompts (>1024 tokens) are memory/kv-bound; p99 increases sharply with concurrency due to slot contention and KV cache eviction paths.
- There is a narrow sweet spot (concurrency 6–12, prompt length 128–256) where both p50/p90 latency and cost-per-query are minimized for our standard GPU pool on a single model variant.

Experiment setup (concise)
- Workload: synthetic conversational sessions, warm-started for 50% of traffic, cold-start for 50%; each session issues a single generate call with variable prompt length.
- Model: open-llama-70b-quant (representative quantized 70B variant used for public perf docs).
- Hardware: single A100-80GB slot (dedicated pool config), kernel config: vectorized attention kernels v2, KV cache enabled.
- Measurement: 30-minute runs per cell, 95% CI approximated by three repeats. Metrics: p50, p90, p99 latency (server-side), amortized cost-per-query (compute tokens * hourly gpu-rate / effective throughput), energy proxy (joules-per-token estimated from platform power logging).
- Batching policy: continuous batching with 50ms aggregation window where applicable; dynamic slot sizing enabled for concurrency > 12.

Definitions
- Prompt length = input tokens before generation (does not include generation length).
- Concurrency = number of simultaneous session requests issued to the same slot pool.
- Amortized cost-per-query = (GPU cost per second) / (queries per second) normalized to $/query. We assume base GPU hourly cost = $3.80 for A100 (internal list price adjusted).

ASCII Mosaic: p90 latency (ms) heatmap by prompt-length (rows) x concurrency (cols)
Legend: . = < 50ms, : = 50-100ms, * = 100-250ms, # = 250-500ms, X = >500ms
Columns: concurrency -> [1,2,4,8,12,16,24]
Rows: prompt len -> [16,32,128,256,512,1024,2048]

  Concur |  1  2  4  8 12 16 24
  -------+----------------------
  16     |  .  .  :  :  *  *  #
  32     |  .  :  :  *  *  *  #
  128    |  :  :  *  *  *  #  X
  256    |  :  *  *  *  #  #  X
  512    |  *  *  *  #  #  X  X
 1024    |  *  *  #  #  X  X  X
 2048    |  #  #  X  X  X  X  X

Interpretation notes for heatmap
- The grid shows a clear transition: small prompts stay in the sub-100ms band until we aggressively pack concurrency; long prompts quickly hit the #/X bands as KV eviction and memory thrash kick in.
- The best practical p90 region (greenish in internal viz) is around prompt length 128–256 and concurrency 4–12.

Cost-per-query surface (sample cells) — $/query (rounded)
- (16 tokens, conc=1): $0.00012/query
- (32 tokens, conc=4): $0.00009/query
- (128 tokens, conc=8): $0.000065/query  <-- 40% cheaper than 16-token single concurrency
- (256 tokens, conc=8): $0.000058/query  <-- sweet spot observed
- (1024 tokens, conc=12): $0.00021/query
- (2048 tokens, conc=8): $0.00048/query

Energy proxy (J/token estimate)
- Small prompts: ~0.045 J/token (fixed kernel overhead prominent)
- Mid prompts (128–512): ~0.018–0.025 J/token (amortization across compute-heavy decode phase)
- Long prompts (>1024): ~0.031–0.055 J/token (memory churn increases energy per token)

Micro-charts: throughput vs concurrency (text bullets)
- Concurrency 1→4: throughput scales ~3.1x (near-linear) for prompts >=128.
- 4→12: scaling diminishes (1.6x) due to batching saturation and contention.
- >12: throughput plateaus or degrades for prompt lengths >512 due to preemption and slot thrash.

Operational implications
- For PLG public API: default max-concurrency per-client should be set to 12 for mid-length conversational workloads to balance latency and cost; surface a ‘fast’ tier that restricts concurrency to 4 but gives lower p50 for tiny prompts.
- For Dedicated pools: recommend autoscaling target windows that favor horizontal slot growth (add slots) over vertical increase in concurrency beyond 12 for long-turn workloads; pre-warm KV caches for long-session cohorts.
- For Private deployments: provide guidance for memory headroom (reserve +12% for KV overhead when average prompt >512 tokens).

Developer-facing collateral copy (2–3 lines)
- "Find the sweet spot: most chat-style workloads reach lowest p90 and $/query in the 128–256 prompt-length band at moderate concurrency (6–12). Avoid pushing very long prompts into high-concurrency slots — latency and cost both increase nonlinearly."

Unresolved questions & next steps (actionable)
- Re-run with alternative quant profiles (8-bit vs 4-bit) to quantify marginal gains in the high-length, high-concurrency cells (INF-821).
- Add multi-model routing test (fallback to smaller model variant under p99 stress) to see graceful-degrade economics.
- Produce a small public-friendly one-pager (2 panels) for Solutions Eng highlighting quick tuning knobs for customer onboarding.

Appendix: quick methodology caveats
- We used synthetic sessions to isolate prompt-length effects; user-driven session cadence can alter KV hit rates and thus the curves.
- Amortized cost uses internal list GPU prices; customer billing may differ (multi-tenant, reserved discounts).
- Latency measured server-side (excluding network tail for global customers).

Notes to reviewers
- Please call out if you want numerical tables for p50/p90/p99 per-cell (we have raw CSVs attached to PR #1427).
- Priority: finalize a small visualization and an internal blurb for the Operations runbook by July 14.

End of draft.
